rubric.note: Ratings are the maintainer's judgment on a 1-10 scale, not measurements. Weights: usefulness for day-to-day engineering and business-document work 40%, runtime and context cost 20% (cheaper is better), risk 20% (safer is better), maturity and upkeep 10%, uniqueness versus overlapping tools 10%. Vendor benchmark claims are reported as claims unless a measurement is named.

items.name: Matt Pocock skills
items.what: Small, composable engineering skills: grilling a requirement, writing a spec, TDD, diagnosing bugs, handoffs, codebase design.
items.impact: Improves requirement clarity and verification before code is written. Works with any model because each skill is a short prompt.
items.activation: Cold. Load grill-me or grilling when a request is ambiguous; tdd and diagnosing-bugs for code changes; handoff when a session must be resumed. The setup skill edits CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and must only run on explicit request.
items.rating_note: High quality and small. Overlaps with other planning and TDD skills, so use one per task.

items.name: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
items.what: Lifecycle skills from define to ship: spec-driven development, planning, incremental implementation, TDD, debugging, review, security hardening, CI/CD, documentation.
items.impact: Gives an agent checklists and quality gates for each engineering phase.
items.activation: Cold. Pick by phase through the code profile. Its hooks folder is for plugin mode and is not wired by this project.
items.rating_note: Broad and well structured, but largely overlaps with other process skills. Loading all of it hot would crowd the skill listing.

items.name: Ponytail
items.what: Makes the agent write the smallest correct change and delete code instead of adding it, without dropping validation, error handling, security or tests.
items.impact: Smaller diffs and fewer speculative abstractions. The maintainer reports -53% code and -45% tokens on its own 39-task benchmark (vendor claim, not reproduced here).
items.activation: Cold: read the ponytail skill before writing or changing code. Optional hooks inject a mode at session start; static review found no network access and no install script.
items.rating_note: Fits a minimal-code policy. Value is smaller if your own rules already say the same.

items.name: Founder skill
items.what: Eleven skills that stress-test a business before launch: board review, marketing, CFO view, consumer panel, pricing, offer, competitors, brand, operations, plan.
items.impact: Structured critique of a business idea. Output is model opinion, not market data.
items.activation: Cold, business profile. Pair with a step that cites dated sources for competitors and prices.
items.rating_note: Useful framing; do not present its numbers as facts.

items.name: Diagram design
items.what: Draws 44 diagram types as one self-contained HTML and SVG file, with brand onboarding and export scripts.
items.impact: Architecture, sequence and quadrant diagrams for documentation without Mermaid or an image service.
items.activation: Cold, docs profile. Python helper scripts run only when the skill is used.
items.rating_note: One skill, low context cost, clear output.

items.name: Graphify
items.what: Builds a queryable knowledge graph of code, docs, schemas and PDFs. Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter; documents and media need a model.
items.impact: Answers structural questions about a repository or document set without grepping. A local run on a small package produced a 107-node graph with no model calls.
items.activation: Tool, research profile. Install from the vetted source with the lockfile. Do not run its global install: it edits the user-level instruction file. Extraction with a model key sends file contents to that provider.
items.rating_note: Good for mixed material. Overlaps with a code-only graph server.

items.name: codebase-memory-mcp
items.what: Native code-intelligence server: indexes a repository into a graph and answers structural queries (search, callers, architecture) locally with no model calls.
items.impact: Cheaper navigation of large repositories. A smoke test indexed a small repo into 363 nodes and 1,404 edges and answered symbol and caller queries.
items.activation: Tool. Register as an MCP server per project when a repository is large. Use the release binary with its checksum and attestation verified; the bundled installer rewrites configuration for about 30 agents and should be run with --skip-config.
items.rating_note: Native Windows ARM64 build, no telemetry found, strong fit for big repos.

items.name: Moli
items.what: Headless browser engine for agents: fetch pages as markdown, JSON or screenshots, search, and expose a CDP or WebDriver server.
items.impact: Fast page reading without a full browser. A test fetched a repository README in under a second.
items.activation: Tool plus three cold skills, research profile. Always pass --block-private-networks for agent-driven fetches. The skills tell the agent to run remote install one-liners: ignore those lines and install the release binary yourself after checking its hash.
items.rating_note: Capable, but it embeds a JavaScript engine that runs page code, and platform browser tools already cover most uses.

items.name: RTK
items.what: CLI proxy that condenses the output of common developer commands before the model reads it. A hook rewrites Bash commands to their rtk equivalent.
items.impact: Measured on six git commands: 164,762 characters became 48,158 (-71%); no saving on git log --oneline. Exit codes were preserved. The hook added about 200 ms per call on an emulated x64 build.
items.activation: Always-on hook candidate. Install the hook only (no instruction file edit). For review or security work re-run the exact command through rtk proxy to see the unfiltered output.
items.rating_note: Largest measured saving of the set. Condensed diffs can hide detail, so keep an escape hatch.

items.name: Context Mode
items.what: MCP server and hooks that sandbox large tool output, index it for search, and track session state across context compaction.
items.impact: Can keep large outputs out of the context window and preserve task state. Not enabled in the maintainer's setup.
items.activation: Disabled by default here. Static review found it appends a hook to the user settings file on every MCP start, rewrites Bash commands such as curl and gradle into echo, registers 16+ hook entries and ships minified bundles. It overlaps with RTK on Bash output; run only one of them per matcher. Elastic License 2.0: do not redistribute inside another product.
items.rating_note: Strong idea, invasive implementation. Revisit when its hook behavior is opt-in.

items.name: API Anything
items.what: Learns a website's own requests and saves them as operations an agent can call over MCP, CLI or TypeScript.
items.impact: Replaces repeated browser driving with direct calls to sites you are allowed to automate.
items.activation: Inert by default. It imports and decrypts browser cookies and stores sessions in plaintext. Use only on sites you own or may automate, with a dedicated browser profile, a restricted data folder, and per-call approval of its login and call tools. Never let an agent run its INSTALL.md.
items.rating_note: Powerful and risky; terms-of-service exposure on logged-in sites.

items.name: Reverse API Engineer
items.what: Captures a site's traffic as a HAR file and has a model write a typed API client for the endpoints it uses.
items.impact: Speeds up building clients for services you are authorized to integrate with.
items.activation: Inert by default. Agent mode runs with permission checks bypassed and sends captured cookies and tokens to the model provider. Disposable environment, authorized targets only.
items.rating_note: Niche, and the default permission posture is too loose for a workstation.

items.name: REA
items.what: Reverse-engineering toolkit exposed through one MCP server: native binaries, Electron and JavaScript apps, Android, firmware, runtime tracing.
items.impact: Helps understand software you are allowed to analyze. Exposes ADB, process tracing and decompilers to the agent.
items.activation: Inert by default and only inside a virtual machine. Its setup command writes other clients' configuration; register the MCP entry by hand.
items.rating_note: Rarely needed and high blast radius.

items.name: OmniRoute
items.what: Local AI gateway that routes requests across many model providers, including free tiers.
items.impact: It does not extend a subscription's usage limit: it sends prompts to other providers, so every prompt leaves your machine. Using a consumer subscription token through a third party is reported to violate Anthropic's terms.
items.activation: Not installed. Consider only for non-sensitive work with your own API keys.

items.name: TensorFlow
items.impact: Not part of an orchestrator. Transformers v5 supports PyTorch only.
items.activation: Not installed. Fine-tuning is documented separately for a cloud environment.

items.name: Transformers
items.what: Model definitions and training utilities for text, vision and audio models.
items.impact: The practical route to fine-tune a small classifier; needs a PyTorch backend and, ideally, a GPU.
items.activation: Not installed locally. Documented for cloud use.
